title: API contract migration guide — sprint notes
body:
Purpose:
This sprint note captures a pragmatic playbook for making breaking or non-breaking API contract changes across Redwood SDKs (JS/TS, Python, Go) while minimizing disruption to customers and internal consumers. This doc is intentionally tactical — checklist style plus experiments to validate the approach during the next Dedicated -> Hosted rollout cycle.

Scope and constraints:
- Focus: client-side SDK surface (request shapes, typed clients, helper conveniences), server-side API compatibility requirements, and migration signals (telemetry, errors).
- Exclude: model weights or runtime kernel changes (handled by serving-runtime).
- Must support both hosted and dedicated customers; private deployments get opt-in communication.
- Timeboxed experiments during sprint: feature-flagged canary + 2-week deprecation windows for small renames.

High-level migration patterns (recommended):
1) Additive-only (safe): add optional params, new response fields, new helper methods. Backward compatible; no SDK bump required for consumers if defaults are stable.
2) Deprecate-and-soft-redirect: mark property/endpoint deprecated, keep behavior, emit telemetry and deprecation headers for 90 days, then remove in a later major.
3) Rename with alias shim: introduce new name, keep old name as alias that maps to new behavior and emits telemetry. Remove alias in a major release after notice.
4) Breaking-change (semantic or contract-level): require coordinated SDK bump with release notes, migration snippets, and canary rollout. Only for changes that cannot be handled by shims.

Versioning strategy (applied to both SDK and API):
- API surface: semver-like with explicit contract-major (breaking changes). Use header X-RI-API-Version for server contracts.
- SDKs: follow major.minor.patch. Any breaking contract change increments major and requires migration guide and at least 2 weeks of opt-in preview.
- Minor/patch releases can include helpers and non-breaking additions.

Deprecation and notice policy:
- Small non-critical deprecations: minimum 30 days notice + telemetry flags.
- Medium risk (behavioral): 60–90 days + migration guide + docs examples.
- High risk (data/semantics): 90+ days + customer outreach + sales/CS runbook.

Telemetry and signals to collect (must be instrumented before change):
- Deprecation header hits: count of requests using deprecated fields/names (by API key).
- Client-side warnings: number of SDKs logging warning at runtime (aggregate by version).
- Error spikes: 4xx/5xx delta post-change by route and client version.
- SDK mismatch rate: requests with incompatible version in agent header.
- Canary error budget burn: measured per region/provider across first 48–72h.

Testing matrix (minimum):
- Matrix dims: SDK versions (last 3 majors), API contract versions (current and canary), runtime (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Unit tests: generated contract tests using schema fakes for request/response shapes.
- Integration tests: e2e harness with a traffic replay (use the existing local-llm-sim infra). Tag as flaky if timing-sensitive.
- Migration smoke-run: a small corpus of prompts + existing customer prompt set (anonymized) run against canary and main.

Rollout playbook (canary -> staged -> full):
1) Feature branch: introduce shim + opt-in flag in SDK and backend.
2) Internal canary: ship SDK with experimental flag to internal dogfood orgs and a set of early customers. Monitor telemetry for 72h.
3) Public preview: release SDK patch/minor with opt-in, announce via changelog + beta docs.
4) Gradual enforcement: after telemetry thresholds met, flip opt-out flag in backend for a subset of traffic (10% -> 50% -> 100%).
5) Removal window: once usage of old contract < 1% for 30 days, schedule removal in next major.

SDK release and packaging guidance:
- JS/TS: publish canary tags (npm dist-tag preview-<YYYYMMDD>) and a stable major on major bumps. Keep agent string to include major+minor+preview.
- Python: use pre-release wheels (rc), support both pip install "redwood==2.0.0rc1" and opacity in agent header.
- Go: follow Go modules, provide clear migration README in repository root.
- Release PR checklist (for SDK owners): update changelog, add migration snippet(s), add deprecation header tests, add telemetry integration, add quickstart for preview.

Customer communication plan:
- Changelog entry + migration guide (examples for node/python/go).
- In-console banner for affected customers with link to preview opt-in.
- CS playbook for high-risk customers: reach out 2+ weeks before removal.
- Email cadence: preview announcement -> reminder -> final removal notice.

Reviewer checklist for PRs that change contracts:
- [ ] Schema diff attached and human-readable description.
- [ ] Tests for old + new contract shapes pass.
- [ ] Deprecation headers emitted for old names where applicable.
- [ ] Telemetry hooks added (metrics and log markers).
- [ ] Docs + quickstart examples updated for both old and new.
- [ ] Migration snippet included and validated in sample-apps repo.
- [ ] Changelog entry drafted.

Sample migration snippets (conceptual) — include in final guide:
- JS shim example: add property alias with runtime warning + deprecation header call to telemetry endpoint.
- Python: decorator-based warning at call time for renamed kwargs.

Experiment plan for next sprint (actionable):
A) Pick small rename: request param `context_window` -> `max_context_tokens` in text.generate helper. Implement alias + runtime warning, instrument telemetry, roll to internal canary (Mar 17–Mar 19), collect signal (Mar 20), iterate.
B) Deprecation header prototype: backend adds X-RI-Deprecation: field=context_window;expires=2026-06-01. SDKs surface a warning via logger. Verify metrics pipeline captures header counts.
C) Migration snippets: add two examples to /developer-experience/samples/migration-examples in monorepo.

Open questions / discussion items:
- Can we get customer-facing console banners for preview opt-ins without additional infra? (Sofia to follow up with console-and-rollouts team.)
- What threshold do we use to consider a shim safe to remove? 1% usage for 30 days is provisional — too aggressive? (CS input required.)
- Private deployments: how to enforce deprecations where customers control the control plane? Proposed: provide a CLI migration helper and extended deprecation window (180 days).

Immediate next steps (this sprint):
- Marcus: prototype telemetry header and verify pipeline (DEVEXP-312).
- Aisha: draft migration guide skeleton + sample snippets (PR target Mar 21).
- Evan: create canary release for JS SDK with alias + opt-in flag (npm preview tag).
- Priya: update PR checklist in repo and add testing matrix template.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep migration examples tiny and copy-paste friendly. Teams hate long migration scripts.
- Use customer prompts where possible for smoke runs — anonymize + store reproducible seeds.
- Avoid too many simultaneous contract changes in a single major — customers will hate multi-step migrations.

References / links (working):
- Jira: DEVEXP-312 (telemetry), DEVEXP-333 (migration snippets), SDK-PR-487 (JS shim), INFRA-947 (traffic replay infra).
- Sample PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/487
- Console rollout thread: #console-rollouts on Slack (see pinned messages).

End of sprint note. This is a working doc — expect gaps and TODOs. Will convert to a public migration playbook once experiments complete and we get CS + console sign-off.
summary: Sprint notes and playbook for safely changing API contracts across Redwood SDKs — telemetry hooks, deprecation policy, canary rollout steps, and migration snippets.
